analysis:
Both supplied units are base-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md, a documentation-only file. The patch excerpt shows documentation additions only: a paragraph on out-of-order completed observations in EnginePerformanceMeasurements.Rate (freshness anchored to the newest observation) and a section on TTFT admission estimator corrections, including the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 revert switch. No executable code, config or authorization paths change in the supplied evidence, so there is no direct security regression.

Relevant threat context. The base text describes Nemotron Super prefix reuse partitioned by authenticated cache scope (T-041). It says there is no reuse without a scope, and image prefix identity is bound to evaluated features. The base text also covers media memory admission and ingress limits. The diff does not alter these statements in the visible hunks.

Uncertainties for later passes:
1. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the full text of the estimator-correction section (head lines 1123-1183) was not seen. It could describe code changes to deadline admission or performance evidence. Those would affect availability or routing but not confidentiality.
2. Freshness anchoring to the newest observation affects capacity and performance evidence. It is not an authorization or encryption control. Any actual code change should be checked for manipulation of heartbeat or routing evidence by a malicious provider (ADV-001). The doc says a heartbeat snapshot alone never renews evidence, which is a reasonable control.
3. The DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES env var is an operator-local switch and does not alter trust boundaries.

No finding is raised, as documentation-only changes in the visible evidence do not weaken any threat-model mitigation. I flag the truncated patch as a coverage limit.
